review_scope: Technical comparison of all 23 composed station frames against the merged release-dream packet. The largest mean RGB difference was 9.04 / 255. The visible layouts and material boundaries were preserved. Scope is the physical surface run.

images.observation: Casing, brass dial, pipework and concrete floor remain distinct in both views.
Cabinet glass, timber and the clear doorway match the paired view.
Wall tile joints and the narrow utility run remain visible beside the fixture.
The station still frames a dark brick close-up. Review is limited to the visible masonry.
Furniture, floorboards and the slatted window retain their distinct surfaces.
The lamp reveals ceramic joints and the curtain beside the companion.
The furnishings and floor match. Wall and hanging light exposure vary slightly.
The window trim, reading shelf and floorboard spacing remain legible.
The wall highlight shifts in intensity. Cabinet, hob and floor remain visible.
The open panel, individual fuses and wall mounting remain legible.
The low angle still leaves the underside dark, with tile and the timber edge visible.
The shelf and curled form remain visible in the dark framing.
Beam, frames and the shelf edge retain the same positions under the warm spill.
Brass compartment plates and the dark timber facing match the paired view.
Ribs, window treatment and wall finish remain distinct around the foreground figure.
The stair guard, roof door and wainscot retain their shape and finish.
The tank skin, supports and parapet retain their silhouettes against the sky.
Terminal casework, notices and floor remain visible as spill intensity changes.
Tile joints and the fixture remain clear under the stronger local light.
The residue and floor plank direction stay legible inside the lamp footprint.
The installed form and surrounding floor remain in view under the moving light.
The fitted appliances and counter finish match. Small loose particles vary in the capture.
The station face and adjacent handle still read. The orange wall splash is weaker.
